title: She prepared for something… she had never seen.
paragraphs: She prepared for something… she had never seen.

No proof.
No pregnancy.
No promise fulfilled.
What kind of faith sets the table… when there is no food?
What kind of woman builds space for a miracle… while living in emptiness?
What kind of heart says “Yes, Lord”… before God says “Now”?

And if we’re honest—
most of us would have quit where she started.
Because let’s not romanticize her story.
This wasn’t soft background music and gentle prayers.
Year after year, she was provoked, mocked, and reminded of what she could not produce (1 Samuel 1:6–7).

Going to worship…
and leaving more broken than when you came.

Believing…
while watching others receive what you begged God for.
That’s where many people are right now.

Smiling in public.
Bleeding in private.

When waiting turns into shame,
shame starts whispering lies.

“You’re not enough.”
“You’re being punished.”
“God is withholding because you’re unworthy.”

And slowly…
faith starts to rot into comparison.
Prayer turns into performance.
Worship becomes heavy.
“She was deeply distressed and prayed to the Lord and wept bitterly.” — 1 Samuel 1:10

No filters.
No pretending.
No polished prayers.
Some scholars interpret Hannah’s prayer as one of the most emotionally transparent cries in Scripture—a model not of perfection, but of dependence.
And then… she did something even more radical.
“If You give me a son, I will give him back to You.” (1 Samuel 1:11)
She surrendered the blessing… before she received it.

Because pride says:
“I’ll trust God after He proves Himself.”

But humility says:
“I belong to God—even if He never gives me what I want.”
Some of us don’t struggle with barren wombs.

We look full on the outside…
but empty inside.
We chase success, attention, relationships, validation—
yet still feel like something is missing.
Because the deepest barrenness is not physical.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23

Not just bad behavior—
a broken nature.

Work harder.
Be better.
Do more.
Because you cannot produce what only God can give.
And this is where the story shifts.
Because God didn’t just answer Hannah with a child.
He answered humanity with a Savior.
“But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth His Son…” — Galatians 4:4
At the cross, He carried your shame.

Every silent insecurity.
Every hidden failure.
Every “why not me” moment.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24

Not by performance.
But by repentance and faith.
Hannah teaches us how to wait.
Jesus teaches us how to be made whole.

Are you preparing your life around God…
or waiting for God to adjust to your plans?

Are you worshiping the Giver…
or just chasing the gift?

Are you holding onto control…
or surrendering even what you don’t yet have?
Because here’s the truth that will set you free:
God is not just preparing the promise for you.
He is preparing you for the promise.
Hannah walked away from that moment of prayer without a child.
“Her face was no longer sad.” — 1 Samuel 1:18
And when the answer finally came—
“In due time Hannah conceived and bore a son…” — 1 Samuel 1:20
Because once you’ve truly encountered God…
Even if your specific prayer is not answered the way you expect—
Jesus is still the greater Yes.
“For all the promises of God find their Yes in Him.” — 2 Corinthians 1:20

Bring your shame.
Bring your waiting.
Bring your emptiness.

“Lord, even before I see it… I trust You.
Even before I hold it… it’s Yours.
Even before You answer… I surrender.”
